batch_context: Profile2 context includes PC/opcode/disassembly, pre/post registers, real memory accesses, boundaries, gap and completion. Reuse instruction facts for events already returned by context. For a small region needing state, start with a bounded window, e.g. --at-ev 0 --before 0 --after 39 --limit 40. Use instructions for wider code-only navigation; context covers only its returned events. Repeat --at-ev; --before 0 --after 0 selects points in one validated scan. Default registers vary by instruction. Repeated --reg selects the same explicit views on every row and replaces defaults; include all needed operand/changed views when merging context with extra states, or use a small point-only batch. Reuse pre/post at the exact event; null post means unobserved completion. Pagination counts describe query rows; capture metadata describes the full stream through END/suffix.
memory_checkpoints: Profile2 mem-state: one --range B,L plus repeated --checkpoint E:pre or E:post shares one full validated scan. Do not mix with --at-ev/--phase. Request order and duplicates are retained. checkpoints-v1 data groups identify ev/phase/pc/instruction_completion/gap and contain byte rows. --limit/--offset apply bytes per checkpoint; at most 64 checkpoints and 4096 returned byte cells in total, no clamping. meta.total/shown count aggregate byte cells; meta.next advances all groups together. An unobserved post is unknown; pre values and global gaps retain their normal semantics. With --json, repeat --range to group disjoint or overlapping ranges in one scan. ranges-checkpoints-v1 returns range_base, range_size and checkpoints in each range group; byte limits apply per range and the whole page cap is 4096 cells.
compact_context: Optional --compact --json: columns-v1, page-local register_sets; Resolve page-local fields and register sets using meta.columns and meta.register_sets. Default named JSON; tools.context_format can select columns-v1. Tiny pages may grow.
metadata_reuse: Reuse fields already present in results.meta for the same unchanged trace (e.g. code_base/data_base/scope). Use stat for missing metadata or detailed format/profile/gap diagnostics. Keep addresses tied to their trace; unknown or absent fields are not zero.
rejections: Rejected attempts are recorded; limits are never silently clamped.
trace_formats: Structured GTSW/GTSC. Execution-state queries use profile2; last-writers retains structured write-evidence profile1. Historical text/GTB2 and its command families are retired; use a frozen older CLI for archived data.
compact_memory_access: Profile2 mem-access supports optional --compact --json: columns-v1 arrays with meta.columns and rw-indexed meta.value_sources. Each page retains all access facts, unknown nulls, pagination and full-input validation. Resolve row fields and value sources using meta.columns and meta.value_sources. Default named JSON; tiny pages may grow. Mixed write-source pages return named rows with meta.compact_fallback=mixed_write_sources to preserve provenance.
compact_memory_state: Profile2 mem-state supports optional --compact --json for single/batch snapshots: hex-v1 frames contain address/size/data_hex and per-byte sources. null source is unknown (00 placeholder); [observed_ev,pc_index] is known, with PCs in page-local meta.pc_table. Limits/counts still measure bytes; all per-byte observations, checkpoint fields, gaps and full validation remain. Resolve each known byte through its source pair and meta.pc_table. Default named JSON; tiny pages may grow.
memory_byte_runs: Profile2 find-value FILE --bytes HEX supports optional --across-events: match1..64 known bytes at adjacent increasing addresses across events. With --read/--write, known disjoint opposite accesses may be skipped; unknowns, gaps, overlaps and selected address/direction changes break runs. This searches historical recorded access sequences, not current memory or last writers. ev/access_index/byte_offset identify the first byte; last_ev/last_access_index identify the last byte. Hits are ordered by completion byte, then pattern order; pagination is per pattern. An unpositioned gap retains only intra-instruction matches without skipped accesses. --context N adds bounded endpoint windows for the first hit. Default --bytes remains within one instruction. Reordered stores can yield no hit despite complete content. Locate/disambiguate a shorter prefix, use mem-access --range B,L to choose the last required observation E, then mem-state --range B,L --checkpoint E:post before later gaps.
